paragraphs.source_en: Only in the past few days had Mitsunari become aware of his mistake. Although the enemy had already advanced as far as Akasaka, they had inexplicably remained in place. Mitsunari had mistakenly assumed that they would not attack Ōgaki Castle but meant to seize his headquarters at Sawayama Castle in one swift stroke, and so he had hurriedly withdrawn. Yet the enemy still made no move, and the dread and terror he had felt at Sawayama continued to churn within his mind.

units.source_en: Only in the past few days had Mitsunari become aware of his mistake.
units.source_zh: 对于自己的失误，三成近几日才觉察到。

units.source_en: Although the enemy had already advanced as far as Akasaka, they had inexplicably remained in place.
units.source_zh: 尽管敌军已进攻到赤坂，令人不解的是，他们却按兵不动。

units.source_en: Mitsunari had mistakenly assumed that they would not attack Ōgaki Castle but meant to seize his headquarters at Sawayama Castle in one swift stroke, and so he had hurriedly withdrawn. Yet the enemy still made no move, and the dread and terror he had felt at Sawayama continued to churn within his mind.

ja.t: とそうとしているのだと

units.source_zh: 三成误以为他们并不会进攻大垣城，单是想一鼓作气拿下自己的大本营佐和山城，便急匆匆撤退，但敌人却依然没有动静，他在佐和山时感受到的战栗和恐怖，至今还在他脑海里翻腾。

paragraphs.source_zh: 对于自己的失误，三成近几日才觉察到。尽管敌军已进攻到赤坂，令人不解的是，他们却按兵不动。三成误以为他们并不会进攻大垣城，单是想一鼓作气拿下自己的大本营佐和山城，便急匆匆撤退，但敌人却依然没有动静，他在佐和山时感受到的战栗和恐怖，至今还在他脑海里翻腾。

paragraphs.source_en: Ieyasu has outwitted me! They must be waiting for Ieyasu to arrive!

units.source_en: Ieyasu has outwitted me!
units.source_zh: 让家康给算计了！

units.source_en: They must be waiting for Ieyasu to arrive!
units.source_zh: 他们必在等待家康的到来！

paragraphs.source_zh: 让家康给算计了！他们必在等待家康的到来！

paragraphs.source_en: When the truth suddenly dawned on Mitsunari, every hair on his body stood on end. Ieyasu's arrival meant that Uesugi Kagekatsu had not taken the bait laid for him as expected. After his fear subsided, he finally understood everything, but that understanding did not lead him onto a brighter path. He sank into despair and persisted in his error to the bitter end.

units.source_en: When the truth suddenly dawned on Mitsunari, every hair on his body stood on end.
units.source_zh: 三成恍然大悟后，全身汗毛倒竖。

units.source_en: Ieyasu's arrival meant that Uesugi Kagekatsu had not taken the bait laid for him as expected.

ja.t: いつかなかったということだ。

units.source_zh: 家康的到来，说明上杉景胜并没如预期那样，扑向他下好的鱼饵。

units.source_en: After his fear subsided, he finally understood everything, but that understanding did not lead him onto a brighter path.

ja.t: いてくれたわけではなかった。

units.source_zh: 但在恐惧之后，他终于明白一切，但这并未把他拉上光明大道。

units.source_en: He sank into despair and persisted in his error to the bitter end.
units.source_zh: 他陷入绝望，一错到底。

paragraphs.source_zh: 三成恍然大悟后，全身汗毛倒竖。家康的到来，说明上杉景胜并没如预期那样，扑向他下好的鱼饵。但在恐惧之后，他终于明白一切，但这并未把他拉上光明大道。他陷入绝望，一错到底。

paragraphs.source_en: After sending his double on ahead, Mitsunari gathered his thoughts once more: Uesugi Kagekatsu had not taken the bait, and Mōri Terumoto remained hidden in Osaka. Why was that? Was the bait simply not enough to make them take the risk? Did the hot blood of the warrior no longer flow in them?

units.source_en: After sending his double on ahead, Mitsunari gathered his thoughts once more: Uesugi Kagekatsu had not taken the bait, and Mōri Terumoto remained hidden in Osaka. Why was that?

ja.t: てこない。いったいなぜなのか。

units.source_zh: 三成把替身先派了出去，又梳理了一遍思路：上杉景胜未上钩，毛利辉元也躲在大坂不出，这究竟是为何？

units.source_en: Was the bait simply not enough to make them take the risk?
units.source_zh: 难道是诱饵并不足以令他们冒险？

units.source_en: Did the hot blood of the warrior no longer flow in them?
units.source_zh: 难道他们不再有武士的热血？

paragraphs.source_zh: 三成把替身先派了出去，又梳理了一遍思路：上杉景胜未上钩，毛利辉元也躲在大坂不出，这究竟是为何？难道是诱饵并不足以令他们冒险？难道他们不再有武士的热血？

paragraphs.source_en: Had Mitsunari been an ordinary man, he would probably have lowered his banners at once upon realizing the vast gulf between himself and Ieyasu. But he was no ordinary man. How could he give up so easily? From the beginning, he had known perfectly well that Ieyasu's power far surpassed his own, yet he had still sought to oppose him to the end.

units.source_en: Had Mitsunari been an ordinary man, he would probably have lowered his banners at once upon realizing the vast gulf between himself and Ieyasu.
units.source_zh: 三成若是个寻常之人，恐怕在意识到与家康的巨大差距后，自会立刻偃旗息鼓。

units.source_en: But he was no ordinary man. How could he give up so easily?
units.source_zh: 但他非寻常之人，岂能轻易罢手？

units.source_en: From the beginning, he had known perfectly well that Ieyasu's power far surpassed his own, yet he had still sought to oppose him to the end.

ja.t: していた。それでもなお、
しようとしたのである。

units.source_zh: 一开始，他就很是清楚家康的实力远胜于自己，但还是企图与之对抗到底。

paragraphs.source_zh: 三成若是个寻常之人，恐怕在意识到与家康的巨大差距后，自会立刻偃旗息鼓。但他非寻常之人，岂能轻易罢手？一开始，他就很是清楚家康的实力远胜于自己，但还是企图与之对抗到底。

paragraphs.source_en: Stubbornness had cast Mitsunari into an abyss of despair.

units.source_en: Stubbornness had cast Mitsunari into an abyss of despair.
units.source_zh: 固执令三成陷入了绝望的深渊。

paragraphs.source_zh: 固执令三成陷入了绝望的深渊。

paragraphs.source_en: Of all the men around him, Mitsunari deeply respected only the loyal and compassionate Ōtani Yoshitsugu, while Shimazu Yoshihiro's valor inspired his awe. On reflection, only this small handful of men had supported him with unwavering resolve. Those he trusted were extending a helping hand, while those he despised were each kicking him when he was down; yet most of those on whom he had counted proved undependable.

units.source_en: Of all the men around him, Mitsunari deeply respected only the loyal and compassionate Ōtani Yoshitsugu, while Shimazu Yoshihiro's valor inspired his awe.
units.source_zh: 在所有人当中，三成只对有情重义的大谷吉继甚是尊重，对岛津义弘的勇猛感到敬畏。

units.source_en: On reflection, only this small handful of men had supported him with unwavering resolve.

ja.t: えているのは、このわずかな

units.source_zh: 仔细想来，也只有这为数不多的几人在矢志不渝地支持他。

units.source_en: Those he trusted were extending a helping hand, while those he despised were each kicking him when he was down; yet most of those on whom he had counted proved undependable.
units.source_zh: 他信任的人都在援之以手，他鄙视的人则一个个落井下石，但他所指望的人，却多指望不上。

paragraphs.source_zh: 在所有人当中，三成只对有情重义的大谷吉继甚是尊重，对岛津义弘的勇猛感到敬畏。仔细想来，也只有这为数不多的几人在矢志不渝地支持他。他信任的人都在援之以手，他鄙视的人则一个个落井下石，但他所指望的人，却多指望不上。

paragraphs.source_en: Every man has his own strengths. If one fails to see this and measures another's weaknesses against one's own strengths, one will only come to scorn and belittle others.

units.source_en: Every man has his own strengths.
units.source_zh: 人各有所长。

units.source_en: If one fails to see this and measures another's weaknesses against one's own strengths, one will only come to scorn and belittle others.

ja.t: んじるようになるだけだ。

units.source_zh: 看不到这一点，以己之长比人之短，只会让自己对人鄙薄、轻视。

paragraphs.source_zh: 人各有所长。看不到这一点，以己之长比人之短，只会让自己对人鄙薄、轻视。

paragraphs.source_en: Before Mitsunari's eyes arose the scene of his flight to Fushimi Castle while the Seven Generals hunted him down. Perhaps Ieyasu had sincerely protected him then; yet the Seven Generals whom Ieyasu had rebuked were now willing to lay down their lives for him. Ah! Enough—enough! At the thought, Mitsunari was stunned and could not help feeling ashamed of himself.

units.source_en: Before Mitsunari's eyes arose the scene of his flight to Fushimi Castle while the Seven Generals hunted him down.
units.source_zh: 三成眼前竟浮现出自己遭到七将追杀、逃到伏见城时的情形。

units.source_en: Perhaps Ieyasu had sincerely protected him then; yet the Seven Generals whom Ieyasu had rebuked were now willing to lay down their lives for him.

ja.t: してくれたのかもしれない。そして

units.source_zh: 那时的家康，或许乃是真心庇护他，而受家康斥责的七将，今日却愿为家康粉身碎骨。

units.source_en: Ah!
units.source_zh: 唉！

units.source_en: Enough—enough!
units.source_zh: 罢罢！

units.source_en: At the thought, Mitsunari was stunned and could not help feeling ashamed of himself.

ja.t: じずにはいられなかった。

units.source_zh: 想到此，三成愕然，不禁为自己感到羞耻。

paragraphs.source_zh: 三成眼前竟浮现出自己遭到七将追杀、逃到伏见城时的情形。那时的家康，或许乃是真心庇护他，而受家康斥责的七将，今日却愿为家康粉身碎骨。唉！罢罢！想到此，三成愕然，不禁为自己感到羞耻。

paragraphs.source_en: Mōri Terumoto and Uesugi Kagekatsu alike had been nothing more than tools to Mitsunari. He had never considered their true feelings, nor had he ever disclosed his own. Why could he not treat them as he did Ōtani Yoshitsugu—respecting and honoring them sincerely, embracing and winning them over with genuine feeling? Could this be the chief reason they had come to doubt Mitsunari and ultimately chosen to sit on the fence? As Mitsunari pondered this, a chill spread through his entire body.

units.source_en: Mōri Terumoto and Uesugi Kagekatsu alike had been nothing more than tools to Mitsunari. He had never considered their true feelings, nor had he ever disclosed his own.

ja.t: いやったこともなければ、

units.source_zh: 无论是毛利辉元还是上杉景胜，都只是三成的工具，他从未考量过他们的真心，亦未向他们吐露过真情。

units.source_en: Why could he not treat them as he did Ōtani Yoshitsugu—respecting and honoring them sincerely, embracing and winning them over with genuine feeling?

ja.t: させることができなかったのか。

units.source_zh: 自己为何不能像对待大谷吉继那般，以真心去尊之敬之，用真情去容之服之？

units.source_en: Could this be the chief reason they had come to doubt Mitsunari and ultimately chosen to sit on the fence?

ja.t: をうかがうようになった

units.source_zh: 莫非这便是导致他们今日对三成产生怀疑，并最终骑墙而观的最大原因？

units.source_en: As Mitsunari pondered this, a chill spread through his entire body.
units.source_zh: 三成思虑着，只觉全身发冷。

paragraphs.source_zh: 无论是毛利辉元还是上杉景胜，都只是三成的工具，他从未考量过他们的真心，亦未向他们吐露过真情。自己为何不能像对待大谷吉继那般，以真心去尊之敬之，用真情去容之服之？莫非这便是导致他们今日对三成产生怀疑，并最终骑墙而观的最大原因？三成思虑着，只觉全身发冷。

paragraphs.source_en: Though he now understood, at this late hour there was no road back. Mitsunari had entered a blind alley, and his heart was inevitably filled with anguish. Between every line, his distress and sorrow seeped through. His suffering was naturally far greater than that of the commanders who remained wholly unaware of all this.

units.source_en: Though he now understood, at this late hour there was no road back.
units.source_zh: 尽管明白过来，但事到如今，已无退路。

units.source_en: Mitsunari had entered a blind alley, and his heart was inevitably filled with anguish.
units.source_zh: 三成走入了死胡同，心中不免悲苦。

units.source_en: Between every line, his distress and sorrow seeped through.
units.source_zh: 字里行间，处处渗透出烦心愁肠。

units.source_en: His suffering was naturally far greater than that of the commanders who remained wholly unaware of all this.
units.source_zh: 这种苦恼，自比那些对此毫无察觉的武将之苦多出许多。

paragraphs.source_zh: 尽管明白过来，但事到如今，已无退路。三成走入了死胡同，心中不免悲苦。字里行间，处处渗透出烦心愁肠。这种苦恼，自比那些对此毫无察觉的武将之苦多出许多。

paragraphs.source_en: At the end of the letter, Mitsunari still could not resist urging Mōri Terumoto to take the field. But this did not mean he still placed hope in Mōri, nor did he expect Nagamori, after reading his long letter, to resolve to share life and death with him. He simply could not keep himself from writing something. Two days later, Ieyasu arrived.

units.source_en: At the end of the letter, Mitsunari still could not resist urging Mōri Terumoto to take the field.

ja.t: さずにはいられなかった。

units.source_zh: 在信的末尾，三成还是忍不住催促毛利辉元出征。

units.source_en: But this did not mean he still placed hope in Mōri, nor did he expect Nagamori, after reading his long letter, to resolve to share life and death with him. He simply could not keep himself from writing something.

ja.t: みをつないでいたからでも、
したからでもない。ただ、
かずにはいられなかったのだ。

units.source_zh: 但这既非说明他对毛利还心存希望，亦非希望长盛在读了他的长函之后，生出与他生死与共的念头，他只是禁不住想写些什么。

units.source_en: Two days later, Ieyasu arrived.
units.source_zh: 这之后两天，家康便来了。

paragraphs.source_zh: 在信的末尾，三成还是忍不住催促毛利辉元出征。但这既非说明他对毛利还心存希望，亦非希望长盛在读了他的长函之后，生出与他生死与共的念头，他只是禁不住想写些什么。这之后两天，家康便来了。

paragraphs.source_en: Mitsunari sat cross-legged, lost in thought and utterly motionless, even forgetting to trim the charred wick of the lamp. He no longer considered whether the battle would be won or lost; he thought only of what his final moment would be like.

units.source_en: Mitsunari sat cross-legged, lost in thought and utterly motionless, even forgetting to trim the charred wick of the lamp.
units.source_zh: 三成盘腿坐在那里凝思着，一动也不动，连灯花都忘了剔去。

units.source_en: He no longer considered whether the battle would be won or lost; he thought only of what his final moment would be like.

ja.t: してはいなかった。ただ、
がどのようなものになるのか、それだけを

units.source_zh: 如今他已不去思量战事胜负了，他只在想临终的一刻会是何样的情形。

paragraphs.source_zh: 三成盘腿坐在那里凝思着，一动也不动，连灯花都忘了剔去。如今他已不去思量战事胜负了，他只在想临终的一刻会是何样的情形。

paragraphs.source_en: Ōgaki Castle gradually fell silent as the autumn rain beat against the railing.

units.source_en: Ōgaki Castle gradually fell silent as the autumn rain beat against the railing.
units.source_zh: 大垣城内逐渐沉寂下来，秋雨敲打着栏杆。

paragraphs.source_zh: 大垣城内逐渐沉寂下来，秋雨敲打着栏杆。

paragraphs.source_en: Almost all the men and horses had left the castle. Because the movement was secret, they could neither light torches nor allow the horses to neigh; together with the steady autumn drizzle, this made the march still more difficult. Even if the highway near Sekigahara remained dry and level, the newly established camp would likely become a field of mud.

units.source_en: Almost all the men and horses had left the castle.
units.source_zh: 人马几乎全部出城了。

units.source_en: Because the movement was secret, they could neither light torches nor allow the horses to neigh; together with the steady autumn drizzle, this made the march still more difficult.

ja.t: をいななかせることもできない。そのうえ

units.source_zh: 因为是秘密行动，既不能点火把，亦不能让马嘶鸣，再加上霏霏秋雨，行军愈发困难。

units.source_en: Even if the highway near Sekigahara remained dry and level, the newly established camp would likely become a field of mud.
units.source_zh: 即使关原附近的大道干爽平坦，新建的大营恐怕也要变成泥田了。

paragraphs.source_zh: 人马几乎全部出城了。因为是秘密行动，既不能点火把，亦不能让马嘶鸣，再加上霏霏秋雨，行军愈发困难。即使关原附近的大道干爽平坦，新建的大营恐怕也要变成泥田了。

paragraphs.source_en: Listening to the rain beyond the railing, Mitsunari began to mock himself. At some point, fear and impatience had vanished completely. To his disbelief, even his sense of tragic resolve seemed to have disappeared without a trace. The decision reached in council that evening seemed to have become someone else's affair altogether.

units.source_en: Listening to the rain beyond the railing, Mitsunari began to mock himself.
units.source_zh: 倾听着栏外的雨声，三成自嘲起来。

units.source_en: At some point, fear and impatience had vanished completely. To his disbelief, even his sense of tragic resolve seemed to have disappeared without a trace.
units.source_zh: 不知从何时起，恐惧和急躁已全然消失，令他难以置信的是，连悲壮的感觉都似消失殆尽了。

units.source_en: The decision reached in council that evening seemed to have become someone else's affair altogether.

ja.t: になってしまったかのようだった。

units.source_zh: 傍晚时合议作的决定，仿佛完全变成了别家的事情。

paragraphs.source_zh: 倾听着栏外的雨声，三成自嘲起来。不知从何时起，恐惧和急躁已全然消失，令他难以置信的是，连悲壮的感觉都似消失殆尽了。傍晚时合议作的决定，仿佛完全变成了别家的事情。

paragraphs.source_en: Ieyasu had made no particular effort to conceal his line of advance. No matter how Mitsunari maneuvered, Ieyasu would cross Sekigahara and press westward.

units.source_en: Ieyasu had made no particular effort to conceal his line of advance.
units.source_zh: 家康并未刻意隐藏自己的进军路线。

units.source_en: No matter how Mitsunari maneuvered, Ieyasu would cross Sekigahara and press westward.
units.source_zh: 无论三成如何腾挪，家康都将踏过关原，向西进发。

paragraphs.source_zh: 家康并未刻意隐藏自己的进军路线。无论三成如何腾挪，家康都将踏过关原，向西进发。

paragraphs.source_en: Against Ieyasu's methodical advance, the Western Army planned to sever his route of retreat and defeat his forces piecemeal—first from north and south, then from east and west. There appeared to be no flaw whatsoever in this deployment. But the question was this: however flawless the deployment, who could guarantee that it would be carried out without error?

units.source_en: Against Ieyasu's methodical advance, the Western Army planned to sever his route of retreat and defeat his forces piecemeal—first from north and south, then from east and west.
units.source_zh: 对于家康的步步为营，西军的对策乃是切断其归路，先从南北、次从东西对其各个击破。

units.source_en: There appeared to be no flaw whatsoever in this deployment.
units.source_zh: 这种布阵看不出丝毫疏漏。

units.source_en: But the question was this: however flawless the deployment, who could guarantee that it would be carried out without error?

ja.t: できるのか、ということだった。

units.source_zh: 但问题是，尽管布阵毫无疏漏，谁敢保证能毫无纰漏地执行？

paragraphs.source_zh: 对于家康的步步为营，西军的对策乃是切断其归路，先从南北、次从东西对其各个击破。这种布阵看不出丝毫疏漏。但问题是，尽管布阵毫无疏漏，谁敢保证能毫无纰漏地执行？

paragraphs.source_en: The Eastern Army was said to number seventy-five thousand, while the Western Army already mobilized numbered more than one hundred and eight thousand. Thus, so long as morale held, it was only natural that Ishida Mitsunari should sing the song of victory.

units.source_en: The Eastern Army was said to number seventy-five thousand, while the Western Army already mobilized numbered more than one hundred and eight thousand.
units.source_zh: 东军据说合有七万五千人，而已出动的西军就超过十万八千人。

units.source_en: Thus, so long as morale held, it was only natural that Ishida Mitsunari should sing the song of victory.
units.source_zh: 因此，只要保持士气，高奏凯歌的理所当然便是石田三成。

paragraphs.source_zh: 东军据说合有七万五千人，而已出动的西军就超过十万八千人。因此，只要保持士气，高奏凯歌的理所当然便是石田三成。

paragraphs.source_en: At this thought, Mitsunari suddenly laughed. How would later generations judge this battle at Sekigahara? Surely they would regard it as the decisive battle that determined the course of the realm. Judged by the numbers on both sides alone, his achievement was without precedent or sequel. But... Mitsunari shook his head. This was no time to contemplate the outcome. He ordered that Fukuhara Nagataka, who was remaining behind to guard Ōgaki Castle, be summoned.

units.source_en: At this thought, Mitsunari suddenly laughed.
units.source_zh: 想到这里，三成忽然笑了。

units.source_en: How would later generations judge this battle at Sekigahara?
units.source_zh: 后世人会如何评价此关原一战？

units.source_en: Surely they would regard it as the decisive battle that determined the course of the realm.

units.source_en: Judged by the numbers on both sides alone, his achievement was without precedent or sequel. But... Mitsunari shook his head. This was no time to contemplate the outcome.

paragraphs.source_en: Though the Western Army numbered one hundred and eight thousand, once its morale declined, its strength would amount to less than half that number. More than that, the unrest and resentment so easily stirred might continue to swell; while provisions for a hundred thousand men were consumed, so too would the fighting spirit of those hundred thousand be drained away... If matters grew worse, not even a tenth of their strength would remain.

paragraphs.source_en: Mitsunari had never reckoned with such things before. He had never valued men's hearts or respected their virtues; he had merely used schemes to piece together numbers. In this respect, he had succeeded—Tokugawa Ieyasu had only seventy-five thousand men, while he, Ishida Mitsunari, commanded an army of one hundred and eight thousand. Yet among this army of a hundred thousand, how many could truly be trusted?
